answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to hold, not just to create: every account must renew a bond each epoch with work that peers actually grade, so a thousand idle clones cannot simply wander in and wait. Trust spreads like a vine, one attested answer grafting onto the next, and a falcon that hunts alone still needs a verified history before its verdicts count. A sybil farm must pay renewal for every seat while earning nothing, so the cost curve bends against it.
